260-complementary-courses: 18 credits over 3 levels of Arabic. With Introductory Arabic (9 credits), the extra 3 count as electives.
261-program-description: Muslim cultures and societies past and present, their variety, global reach and regional specifics, especially the Middle East, through languages, texts and social life.
261-complementary-courses-18-credits: 3 credits of non-language ISLA at 200; 6 at 300+; 9 at any level, at most 6 non-language at 200 overall. These can come from the Non-ISLA list. Hebrew (JWST 220, 320, 340) counts as non-language.
263-complementary-courses-36-credits: 12–15 credits over 2 levels of one language: Arabic, Persian, Turkish or Urdu (Arabic's two levels are 15).
21–24 more: 3 non-language ISLA at 200, 6 at 300, 6 at 400–500, 6–9 at any level, with at most 6 non-language at 200 overall. Hebrew counts as non-language.
265-program-description: Muslim cultures past and present through texts and social life. Keep program GPA 3.30 and CGPA 3.00.
265-complementary-courses-54-credits: 18–21 credits over 3 levels of one language. 33–36 more: 3 non-language ISLA at 100–200, 12 at 300, 9 at 400–500, 9–12 at any level, at most 9 at 100–200.
267-program-description: Muslim cultures past and present, combined with another Arts discipline. See an adviser in each department. Keep program GPA 3.30 and CGPA 3.00.
267-complementary-courses-33-credits: 12–15 credits over 2 levels of one language. 18–21 more: 3 non-language ISLA at 100–200, 9 at 300, 3 at 400–500, 3–6 at any level, at most 6 at 200.
270-about-the-mcgill-institute-for-the-s: Founded in 1994 with the Bronfman family. Runs an academic program, supports research, and holds public events and annual conferences. Non-partisan.
Teaches adaptive thinking, communication, research, collaboration, leadership and public engagement, with a practical focus.
270-canadian-studies: A broad view of Canada's nature and development, through a minor, major, honours and joint honours.
The Minor encourages bilingualism and critical engagement; the Major focuses on public affairs. For graduate study or a thesis, consider Honours or Joint Honours.
270-indigenous-studies: A minor on the historical, social and cultural sides of Indigenous life in Canada: history, art and culture, indigeneity and gender, and resistance to the state, with core courses plus others from across McGill.
270-quebec-studies: A minor on Québec's past and present, with hands-on experience in a Montréal community organization.
270-generalites-etudes-sur-le-quebec: En français : une concentration mineure interdisciplinaire sur la société québécoise. QCST 200, 300 et 440 relèvent du programme, les autres cours des départements. Travaux et examens en français ou en anglais (français obligatoire au Département des littératures).
Directeur : Pr Pascal Brissette, W130a. Coordonnateur scientifique : Stéphan Gervais, Ferrier 102E. Affaires étudiantes : David Roseman, Ferrier 102G.
271-about-quebec-studies: An interdisciplinary minor on Québec in Canadian and international context. QCST 200, 300 and 440 are the program's own; other courses belong to departments, and not all run yearly. Advisers can recommend, but the choice is yours if you meet prerequisites.
Work and exams in French or English (French only in the Département des littératures).
Director: Prof. Pascal Brissette, Arts 130a. Scientific Coordinator: Stéphan Gervais, Ferrier 102E. Student Affairs: David Roseman, Ferrier 102G.
271-program-description: Canada and its key institutions, with an emphasis on public affairs, outside your other programs' areas.
272-program-description: Multidisciplinary perspectives on Canada and its institutions, focused on public affairs and social and cultural debates, from humanities and social sciences.
273-program-description: The same focus in depth. Apply by December 15 or May 15 with program GPA 3.30 and CGPA 3.00, using forms on the MISC site.
275-program-description: The same focus, combined with another Arts discipline. Apply by December 25 or May 15 with program GPA 3.30 and CGPA 3.00. See an adviser in each department.
276-program-description: Key issues in Indigenous life in Canada: history, art and culture, indigeneity and gender, and resistance.
276-complementary-courses-12-credits: At most 3 at 200, and 6 from any discipline other than INDG.
277-program-description: Québec's history and present, complementing your degree, with a placement in a Montréal community organization arranged with the SEDE Office, and attention to equity, diversity and inclusion. / Un aperçu interdisciplinaire du Québec, avec un stage dans un organisme montréalais.
277-required-courses-cours-obligatoires-: Usual order: QCST 200 in U0 or U1, QCST 300 in U1, QCST 440 in U2 or U3. Complementaries in U1–U3.
277-complementary-courses-cours-compleme: 6 from the core or approved by the Director; 3 taught in French (FRSL allowed); at least 6 at 300+. Choose with the Director.
279-about-international-development: ISID aims to improve lives through research, training and communication for sustainable development, working with NGOs, governments, communities and the private sector.
279-international-development-studies: Interdisciplinary study of developing countries' problems. Most courses above 200 have prerequisites, and some, especially Management, may have no space. Check the Class Schedule.
279-location: 3610 McTavish St., 2nd Floor. Adviser: Lisa Stanischewski.
279-program-description: Inequality, governance, conflict, environment and other challenges. At least 9 of 18 credits at 300+. Some Field Studies courses can count; see the Adviser.
